summary: Former Rowan County electric transmission tower rebuilt on Fox Mountain in 1956; a 1968 plan to close it drew a request to keep it running.

facts.design: Former electric transmission tower, moved from Rowan County and rebuilt on the mountain
facts.status_note: No source after 1968 says whether the tower stayed open, came down, or still stands.

events.note: Reported as due for completion in February 1956, after reconstruction atop the mountain.
Moved from Rowan County to Fox Mountain, Iredell County.
Tower spotted smoke about 2 p.m. (report dated November 22, 1958); a smoke chaser brought the blaze under control.
District forester had indicated the tower would be closed; county commissioners asked that it continue. The outcome is not in the source.

evidence.supports: The tower was formerly an electric transmission tower in Rowan County.
evidence.quote: formerly used as an electric transmission tower in Rowan County

evidence.supports: Mill Power Supply Co. of Charlotte donated the tower to Iredell's forestry service.
evidence.quote: was donated to Iredell's forestry service by Mill Power Supply Co., Charlotte.

evidence.supports: The tower was moved to Fox Mountain and being rebuilt there by Love Valley, Inc., and the Forestry Service.
evidence.quote: It was moved here from Rowan County and is being reconstructed atop the mountain by Love Valley, Inc., and the Forestry Service, he said.

evidence.supports: The new tower was to be completed in February 1956.
evidence.quote: A new fire detection tower atop Fox Mountain in North Iredell County should be completed this month,

evidence.supports: The tower spotted smoke in November 1958.
evidence.quote: Fox Mountain Tower in North Iredell picked up the smoke about 2 p.m.

evidence.supports: A smoke chaser brought the 1958 blaze under control.
evidence.quote: The blaze was brought under control by John Christie, Iredell Smoke chaser

evidence.supports: In 1968 the district forester had indicated the tower would be closed, and commissioners asked that it continue.
evidence.quote: Commissioners passed a resolution requesting the district forester to continue the operation of the Fox Mountain Fire Tower which he had indicated would be closed.

evidence.supports: The department had built more permanent and higher towers.
evidence.quote: the department had constructed more permanent and higher towers which would give 'adequate' detection

evidence.supports: Representatives of volunteer fire departments asked that the tower be continued.
evidence.quote: Representatives from some of the volunteer fire departments were present to ask that the tower be continued.

sources.title: Fox Mountain (North Carolina lookouts, quoting Statesville Record and Landmark reports, 1956-1968)

notes_for_editor: Only one source: a lookout-history site transcribing three 1956-1968 newspaper items. Two searches and the brief's pages found no other record of a tower on this mountain in Iredell County. The 1968 article says closure was indicated, not that it happened. The brief's record had no height, status or agency. Search results for other Fox Mountains (Pennsylvania, California, New York) were not used. The Love Valley Wikipedia page was checked and mentions no tower. The 'agency' fact keeps the 1956 wording (Iredell's forestry service) and is not a verified agency name.
